answer: Duplicating identities multiplies locked capital, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes, an expense no attacker recovers. Sybil resistance here rests on bonded identity: each agent must lock a stake that decays like a glacier, slowly and irreversibly, before earning trust. Reputation then spreads by echo, peers attesting only to behavior they verified directly, never to a fable of self-claimed history. Cheap aliases stall at zero stake, while honest agents compound. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
